newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's first brokerage set up for unlisted stocks.
newsitem.headline: Japan's first brokerage set up for unlisted stocks.

text.p: A brokerage house specialising in trading unlisted Japanese shares was set up on Monday, with the aim of establishing a market for the shares and to provide entrepreneurs with enough funds to run their businesses.

The brokerage, D.Brain Co Ltd, which is due to start business at the end of August, said potential demand for unlisted stocks is strong and that the number of issues it expects to deal in will boom in the next few years.
The company will initially trade eight companies, with the number expected to jump to about 50 by the end of this year.

"We expect the number to be 250 firms next year and 500 firms in the year after that. Eventually we will deal with about 30,000 firms out of a potential 1.3 million firms in the country," said Yoshito Denawa, the founder and an executive director of D.Brain Co Ltd.
The move follows the announcement in late June by regional Japanese brokerage Ark Securities Co Ltd that it would start broking unlisted shares in firms set up by venture capitalists.
Ark Securities, based in Aichi prefecture of central Japan, said it would start the broking operation on July 1 for individual investors.
"We basically deal with shares of companies, if they are challenging and ready to contribute to society," Denawa told a news conference.

"The scale of the fund-raising in the market will hopefully grow to one trillion to three trillion yen in the future," Denawa said, adding that an individual company could raise up 100 to 300 million yen in funds.
"Securities houses receive many queries about unlisted stocks but there is no market where investors can buy such stocks. I'm sure the potential demand is big," he said.
Japan recently lifted a ban on brokerages from trading such shares as a part of the "Big Bang" financial deregulation.
D.Brain, capitalised at 180 million yen, expects to post six million yen in current losses for the financial year to the end of March 1998.
But it expects to post 29 million yen in current profits for 1998/99 and 67 million yen in current profits for 1999/2000.
